claims.text: The initial equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloy is single-phase FCC after thermomechanical processing.
Mechanical-property differences among the candidate alloys are governed by composition-induced variations in stacking fault energy.
Removing Cr from equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni to form equiatomic Mn-Fe-Co-Ni lowers the stacking fault energy.
Lower stacking fault energy reduces the barrier to deformation twinning.
The composition-induced change in stacking fault energy alters dislocation cross-slip behavior.
The Cr-free Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloy will develop more deformation twinning and a greater twin-boundary density than the quinary baseline.
More prevalent deformation twinning enhances strain hardening.
The equiatomic Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloy will have a higher strain-hardening rate than equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni under identical processing and testing conditions.
The equiatomic Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloy will have a higher yield strength than equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni under identical processing and testing conditions.
Enhanced strain hardening caused by deformation twinning increases yield strength.
The proposed mechanism applies only to compositionally varied alloys that remain single-phase FCC and deform primarily through dislocation activity and twinning.
